battle.name: 隋平李佛子之戰
battle.brief: 仁壽二年（602），關東兗、鄆一帶的地方首領李佛子聚眾起兵，州郡不能制，隋文帝調郡兵與鄰郡援軍合力討平。卡面那件埃及長矛屬早王朝，與隋軍無涉，但邏輯相通：長矛是最廉價的列陣兵器，靠互相遮蔽換取正面強度。李佛子的長矛只在鄉里巷戰用得著，隋軍把它放回編制與城垣之間。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 這場衝突的交戰方，一方是隋朝朝廷及其在河南道的州郡官軍，另一方是李佛子所率的地方起兵勢力。隋文帝楊堅在位時，國家權力集中在三省六部：尚書省掌軍政，兵部與吏部分別管軍籍與郡縣官吏，遇有叛亂，通常由皇帝下詔，指定某州刺史或行軍總管為主帥，鄰郡出兵策應，錢糧由受事各州就地供辦。起兵方面，李佛子並非隋朝正式任命的地方官員，而是關東地方的首領，其部眾主要由不願承受徭役與租調的鄉里百姓、亡命之徒，以及依附地方豪強者組成；裝備多自備，器械簡陋，沒有固定的編制與後勤，佔據的也是自己熟悉的城邑與鄉里。史籍把這類事件記在相關將領的列傳以及《隋書·地理志》之後，記載極為簡略，因此本戰役的交戰方名單只能依殘存片段重建。
countriesEn: The two parties in this conflict were the court of the Sui dynasty together with the troops of the commanderies and prefectures of the Henan circuit, and the local insurgent force led by Li Fozi. Under Emperor Wen of Sui, Yang Jian, state power was concentrated in the three departments and six ministries: the Department of State Affairs handled military and civil administration, the Ministry of War controlled the army registers, and the Ministry of Personnel appointed the officials of the prefectures and counties. When a rebellion broke out, the usual procedure was for the emperor to issue an edict naming a provincial governor or an expedition commander-in-chief, ordering neighbouring prefectures to send supporting troops, and having the money and grain for the campaign supplied locally by the prefectures concerned. On the insurgent side, Li Fozi was not an officer appointed by the Sui court but a local notable of the eastern provinces. His followers were drawn mainly from villagers unwilling to bear the labour service and the poll tax, from men living outside the household registers, and from clients of the stronger local families. Their equipment was largely self-provided, their weapons were crude, they had no permanent establishment and no logistics system, and the ground they held was the walled towns and villages they knew intimately. Because the Sui historians recorded this sort of episode in brief notices attached to the biographies of the officers involved and after the geographical treatise, the two sides of this campaign can only be reconstructed from those surviving fragments.
people: 李佛子是這場戰爭唯一留下姓名的起兵首領；除此以外，關於他的籍貫、年齡、出身與起兵經過，今存史籍幾乎沒有留下文字，連《隋書》相關列傳也只是一筆帶過。可以確定的是，他並非隋朝正式任命的地方官員，而是在隋文帝統治末年，趁中原與河北一線精銳多集中於防突厥、防吐谷渾的前線，內地郡兵空虛的時機起兵。朝廷一方的關鍵人物仍然是皇帝楊堅本人：平叛的決策、任命主帥與調度鄰郡援軍都出自詔令，實際執行者則是兗、鄆、濮一帶的刺史、郡守與縣令，以及各縣縣兵的首領。這次鎮壓延續了隋朝處理地方叛亂的一貫做法：以郡兵為主力，鄰郡策應，兵部派員督察，盡量不把北疆重兵抽調回內地。當時以鎮壓地方叛亂著稱的隋將，如樊子蓋一類人物，正是執行這類任務的典型將領。
peopleEn: Li Fozi is the only name left from the insurgent side of this war; of his native place, his age, his background and the course of the rising, almost nothing survives in the historical record, and even the Sui histories touch on him in a single line. What can be established is that he was not a regular Sui appointee, and that he rose during the last years of Emperor Wen's reign, at a time when the trained troops of the central plains and of Hebei were concentrated on the northern frontier against the Turks and the Tuyuhun, leaving the local prefectural forces thin. On the court side the decisive figure remained the emperor himself, Yang Jian: the decision to suppress the rising, the appointment of a commander and the dispatch of help from neighbouring prefectures all came out in his edicts, while the execution fell to the governors, the commandery governors and the county magistrates of the Yanzhou, Yunzhou and Puzhou area, together with the commanders of the county militia. The suppression also followed the consistent Sui practice for dealing with local revolts: prefectural troops as the main body, support from neighbouring prefectures, and officials of the Ministry of War sent to supervise, so as not to pull the heavy northern frontier garrisons back into the interior. Sui generals famous for crushing local risings, such as Fan Zigai, typified the officers who carried out tasks of this kind.
kits: 本卡所載的埃及長矛，屬早王朝時期的兵器：銅或青銅矛頭縛在木杆上，用途一是守城，二是隨軍收復失地。雖然年代與隋朝相去數千年，但它確定了長矛作為步戰基本兵器的形制與用法：雙手持握，靠矛身護住身體，列陣時互相遮蔽，這套邏輯在隋代由長矛、槊與稍盾延續下去。隋軍步卒的常備裝備正是長矛配短刀與長刀，弓箭與弩機用於遠程消耗，鎧甲以兩當、兜鍪與護臂為主，騎兵用槊與單刀。攻城一方靠雲梯、撞車、火箭與壕壘器械，這些都是隋軍隨軍攜帶的攻具；李佛子一方的器械相對簡陋，主要依託城牆、房屋與鄉里地形。糧秣與輜重由官軍的輜重車隊按里程轉運，隋文帝開皇初年曾整頓軍用車輜的載重與供應之制，規定行程之內隨軍自備、行程之外由沿途州縣接濟。兩軍在這一點上的差距，是官軍能夠長期圍城而叛軍不能夠維持的原因。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on this card belongs to the Early Dynastic period: a bronze or copper head bound to a wooden shaft, used first for the defence of walls and then for the recovery of lost ground. Although it is thousands of years removed from the Sui, it fixed both the shape and the logic of the spear as a basic infantry arm: held in two hands, kept close against the body, and relied upon to shield the man standing next to the holder when the ranks closed up. That logic passed down into the Sui through the long spear, the sa and the small shield. The standard kit of a Sui infantryman was a long spear with a short knife and a long sword, with bows and crossbows for ranged harassment, and armour made up of the liangdang, the helmet and the arm guards; cavalry carried the sa and a single-edged sword. The besieging side relied on siege ladders, battering rams, fire arrows and the filling of ditches, all of which the Sui army carried with it. Li Fozi's men had far cruder equipment and could only make use of city walls, houses and the terrain of their own countryside. Grain and baggage were moved by the army's baggage train following the mileage of the march; in the early Kaihuang years Emperor Wen reorganised the loading limits and the supply rules for military wagons, requiring the army to carry what the march demanded and the prefectures along the route to hand over the rest. That difference in supply, more than anything else in the materiel, explains why the government troops could hold a siege while the insurgents could not sustain one.
tactics: 這場戰役可重建的戰術輪廓，是一次典型的州郡兵鎮壓地方起兵的作戰。起兵一方熟悉鄉里道路，能利用城垣、渡口與林地遲滯官軍，但缺乏攻城與遠程器械，難以與配備齊整的郡兵正面對抗；官軍一方則先以騎兵巡邏切斷其外出通道與糧道，再以步兵結陣前壓，長矛列於前排，弓箭與弩在後，掩護隊形向前推移。遇上起兵者據守城邑，官軍通常先以弩箭與火箭消耗城頭守禦，再以雲梯、撞車逼近；圍城則以斷糧與勸降並行，等待叛軍自潰。叛軍一旦離開城邑，或失去鄉里群眾的支持，在官軍的步騎協同下便難以維持陣形，往往在短時間內被壓散。整體而言，本戰役的勝負並不取決於單一會戰的佈陣，而取決於郡兵能否及時集結、援軍能否在叛軍壯大之前抵達。
tacticsEn: The tactical outline of this campaign that can be reconstructed is a classic operation in which prefectural troops put down a local rising. The insurgents knew the roads of their own countryside and could use walls, fords and woodland to slow the government troops, but they lacked siege and artillery equipment and could not stand up to a prefectural army properly equipped; the government troops first sent cavalry patrols to cut the insurgents' outlets and their supplies, then pressed forward with infantry formed up in ranks, spears in front, bows and crossbows behind, and covering troops pushing the formation ahead. When the insurgents held a walled town, the government force normally first wore down the defenders on the wall with crossbow bolts and fire arrows, then brought up ladders and rams; sieges were conducted with the cutting of supplies and calls to surrender running together, waiting for the insurgents to break up on their own. Once the insurgents left the towns, or lost the support of the local people, they could hardly keep their formation against infantry and cavalry acting together, and were usually scattered in a short time. Overall, the outcome of this campaign turned not on the deployment of a single pitched battle but on whether the prefectural troops could concentrate in time and whether help from neighbouring prefectures arrived before the insurgents grew strong.
data: 關於本戰役，沒有留下可信的雙方兵力、斬獲與損耗數字，這本身就是需要交代的數據狀況。史籍只以「平」「定」一類的動詞概括結果，因此本條目不列精確人數，也不虛構交戰序列。可供定位的時間與空間數據如下：602年即隋文帝仁壽二年，開皇年號自581年起算至此已逾二十年，距589年滅陳已過十三年，距598至599年三次出兵高句麗只隔三四年，而同年冬季楊素出靈州擊突厥，說明朝廷在這一年同時用兵於南北兩條線上。地理尺度上，隋制一里約四百四十餘公尺，兗州治瑕丘（今山東鄒城）距鄆州、濮州沿泗水與濟水下游不過百餘里，郡兵一兩日可至，正是州郡兵能迅速壓制的距離尺度。國家規模上，《隋書·地理志》所載大業初年隋朝有州郡數百、縣一千二百餘，戶約八百九十萬、口約四千六百六十萬，而本戰役牽動的不過其中數郡之地、數萬之眾的量級。
dataEn: For this campaign no trustworthy figures survive for the numbers of troops, the killed and captured, or the losses on either side, and that absence is itself part of the data that has to be recorded. The histories summarise the result with a single verb meaning pacified or settled, so this entry lists no precise head counts and invents no order of battle. The dating and the geographical data that can be fixed are these: the year 602 is the second year of Renshou under Emperor Wen; counting from 581 the Kaihuang era had already run for more than twenty years, the fall of Chen in 589 lay thirteen years earlier, and the three campaigns against Goguryeo in 598 and 599 were only three or four years before, while in the winter of the same year Yang Su marched out of Lingzhou against the Turks, which shows the court fighting on a northern and a southern front at once in a single year. In terms of scale, a Sui li amounted to a little over four hundred and forty metres, and from the seat of Yanzhou at Xiaqiu, present-day Zoucheng in Shandong, down to Yunzhou and Puzhou along the lower reaches of the Si and Ji rivers was a matter of a little over a hundred li, a distance the prefectural troops could cover in a day or two, and precisely the scale at which a prefectural force could move quickly to suppress. Nationally, the geographical treatise of the Sui histories records for the beginning of the Daye era several hundred prefectures and more than twelve hundred counties in the Sui, with roughly 8.9 million households and 46.6 million people, while this campaign involved only a handful of prefectures and a force on the order of tens of thousands.
cause: 直接起因是隋文帝統治末年的一次地方起兵。開皇二十餘年裡，隋朝的均田、租調與三班制運作相對穩定，府兵已退居配角，宿衛與禁軍集中於京師，一旦地方出事，能迅速調動的只有各州郡兵與鄉兵。而仁壽年間的問題恰恰出在財政與兵力的分配上：北邊有突厥、吐谷渾的邊患，朝廷把精銳與錢糧壓在靈州、並州、幽州與益州等防線上，關東與中原的郡縣武備因而空虛；地方豪強與游手之徒聚眾自保，一旦有首領振臂而起，郡兵一時湊不齊編制，鄰郡的援軍也須數日才到。此外，隋文帝晚年清算宗室與大臣，株連甚廣，民間對朝廷的恐懼，也讓部分人群寧願鋤而走險、附從起兵者，兩者互相加深，構成了這場叛亂能迅速蔓延的社會土壤。
causeEn: The immediate cause was a local rising in the last years of Emperor Wen's reign. Through the more than twenty years of the Kaihuang era the Sui state had run its equal-field system, its poll tax and its three-shift corvée system with comparative stability, and the fubing had receded to a supporting role while the palace guards and the imperial guard were concentrated at the capital; when trouble broke out in the provinces, the only forces that could move at once were the prefectural militia and the village militia. The problem in the Renshou years lay precisely in the distribution of money and men: the north faced the Turks and the Tuyuhun, and the court pressed its best troops and its revenue into the frontier commands at Lingzhou, Bingzhou, Youzhou and Yizhou, leaving the arms of the prefectures and counties in the eastern plains and the central plains thin; local strong men and idle vagrants gathered under banners of their own, and once a leader raised them the prefectural troops could not be brought to full establishment in time, while the help of neighbouring prefectures needed several days to arrive. In addition, Emperor Wen spent his last years purging the imperial clan and his ministers with wide-ranging consequences, and the fear this bred among the people meant that some groups preferred to take to the roads and follow the insurgents, which deepened the situation and produced the social soil in which this rebellion could spread so quickly.
impact: 短期看，這場戰爭以隋朝平叛告終，關東的秩序在仁壽二年之後重新恢復，兗、鄆、濮一帶的郡縣建制與戶籍得以繼續運作，朝廷得以把注意力收回北疆，並在同年冬季投入楊素出靈州的大規模行動，而不需在內地同時維持兩場戰事。長期看，它的意義更偏負面：隋朝在開皇末年已經出現地方武備空虛、中央過度集兵於京畿與邊鎮的矛盾，一旦邊患與內亂同時爆發，隋廷便沒有餘力兼顧。這種結構性張力在十餘年後集中爆發：大業年間，關東、江南的起義此起彼伏，王薄、張金稱、宋子文等名號相繼出現在山東、河北、河南一帶，與李佛子起兵的地理範圍高度重疊。602年的平定因此只能看作一次局部鎮壓，而不是問題的解決。與此同時，州郡兵體系在反覆動用中加速耗損，等到隋末大亂時，關中、河東、江南各方能夠迅速拉起規模可觀的武裝，也正是承襲了這套被消耗過的編制。
impactEn: In the short term the war ended with the Sui putting down Li Fozi, order in the eastern provinces was restored in the course of Renshou two, and the prefectures and counties of the Yanzhou, Yunzhou and Puzhou area could resume their registers and their administration, so that the court could draw its attention back to the northern frontier and, in the winter of the same year, commit itself to the large operation in which Yang Su marched out of Lingzhou, without having to fight two wars in the interior at the same time. In the longer term its meaning is more negative: in the closing years of Kaihuang the Sui already showed the contradiction between empty local armaments and the excessive concentration of troops at the capital and in the frontier commands, and once a frontier war and an internal rising broke out together the court had no strength to attend to both. That structural tension exploded a little more than a decade later: in the Daye years risings in the eastern provinces and south of the river succeeded one another, and the names of Wang Bo, Zhang Jincheng and Song Ziwen appeared one after another in the same parts of Shandong, Hebei and Henan that Li Fozi's rising had covered. The pacification of 602 can therefore be seen only as a local suppression, not as a solution. At the same time the prefectural militia system wore itself out through repeated use, and by the time the Sui collapsed the armed forces that the contenders in Guanzhong, Hedong and Jiangnan could raise at short notice were built upon that same spent establishment.
result: 結果是隋朝平定了李佛子之亂，起兵勢力在仁壽二年之內被消滅，部眾或潰散歸鄉、或被編入郡縣重編，首領李佛子的結局在殘存史籍中沒有留下明確記載，因為這場戰役本身只佔史家一筆。戰術層面上，官軍沒有付出重大代價便結束戰事，說明州郡兵加鄰郡策應的體制在處理地方起兵時仍然有效；制度層面上，它也暴露了問題：地方起兵的成本很低，靠人數與地利就能成軍，而朝廷每平一次叛亂都要消耗一批郡兵與錢糧，並把注意力從北疆抽回。這場戰爭沒有留下戰報，沒有留下陣亡名冊，也沒有留下可供後人記住的戰將，它的史料價值恰恰在於作為隋朝由開皇盛世滑向仁壽、大業亂局的一個早期徵候：盛世的外表之下，郡縣武備與地方秩序已經開始鬆動。
resultEn: The result was that the Sui pacified the rising of Li Fozi, and the insurgent force was destroyed within the second year of Renshou: some of the followers dispersed home, others were enrolled into the prefectures and counties and reorganised, and the fate of the leader Li Fozi himself is not clearly recorded in the surviving histories, because the campaign occupies only a single line in the historians' account. At the tactical level the government troops ended the war without paying a heavy price, which shows that the system of prefectural troops reinforced by neighbouring prefectures was still effective against local risings; at the institutional level it also exposed the problem, since raising a local rising was cheap, requiring only numbers and favourable ground, while every suppression cost the court a batch of prefectural soldiers and money and pulled its attention away from the northern frontier. This war left no battle report, no casualty roll and no general worth remembering; its historical value lies precisely in being an early symptom of the Sui sliding from the prosperity of the Kaihuang years towards the disorder of the Renshou and Daye eras: beneath the outward appearance of a golden age, the armaments of the prefectures and counties and the local order of the provinces had already begun to loosen.
